kept.corrected_quote: 一回生，二回熟。/ The first time, strange; the second time, familiar.
kept.corrected_meaning: The first time feels strange. The second time, it already feels familiar.
kept.evidence: Pulled the raw text of each zh.wikisource page. (1) 醒世姻緣傳/042, paragraph 34, reads in full: '大凡事體，只怕不做，不怕不會。這魏氏一遭生，兩遭熟，三遭就會，四遭也就成了慣家。' So the candidate silently drops the subject 這魏氏 ('this Mrs. Wei') with no '...'. More important, 'three times you can do it, four times a practiced hand' is not a folk saying. It is the novelist's own extension of the two-step proverb, written about one named character. Crediting the four-step line to 'Chinese saying' is a misattribution. The chapter title is 妖狐假惡鬼行兇 ('a fox spirit poses as an evil ghost to do harm'). Paragraphs 31 to 34 show Mrs. Wei, possessed by the fox spirit, put up a sign as a medium. At first she is too ashamed to do it well. Then she becomes a smooth fake fortune-teller, inventing answers about illness, theft and unborn children for incense money. Later in the chapter a ghost has sex with her. (2) 醒世姻緣傳/025, line 14: '真是「一遭生，兩遭熟」，越發成了相知。' This is a neutral scene: Teacher Xue and Squire Di drink together on a rainy day and become friends. It confirms the two-step form is a stock saying of the period. (3) 民國大竹縣志 (page header: 〔民國〕續修大竹縣志, 民國十七年戊辰春二月出版, i.e. 1928) has the heading 諺語 > 三字, and its list includes the exact line '一回生，二回熟。' next to 先學爬，後學走 and similar sayings. Attribution, year and section are all confirmed for the short form. (4) Not in used_quotes.txt; the Chinese proverbs used so far are 'Iron long fired becomes steel' and 'No one knows how difficult anything is until he has tried to do it', both different.
kept.safety: FAIL for the four-step ch. 42 line as submitted. In context it describes a possessed woman getting skilled at cheating people as a fake spirit medium. That is fraud (crime), it mocks folk religion and mediums, and the chapter also has ghost-sex content. If credited honestly it has to name the novel, which points straight to this scene. The stage-1 line just before it, '大凡事體，只怕不做，不怕不會', is the narrator's lead-in to the same sentence and has the same problem, so do not use it either. PASS for the corrected short form 一回生，二回熟: it is a plain folk proverb in a neutral list of three-character sayings in the 1928 gazetteer, with no war, politics, royalty, crime, disaster or old-age content. On the slide, credit it only as 'Chinese saying', and do not cite or translate the ch. 42 four-step version.
